items.title: 11,000 applications a minute: the AI job application arms race nobody wins
items.pt:
In June 2025, The New York Times reported that LinkedIn was receiving about 11,000 job applications a minute, up 45% in a year (Semafor's summary). One HR consultant in that story got 1,200 responses to a single post within days.

items.title: The AI Product Manager Career Path: Routes In, Skills by Stage, and a 90-Day Plan
items.pt:
Engineers usually ask the question this way: I already ship model-backed features, so is the next step an AI product manager role? Traditional PMs ask a different version: the roadmap now has a copilot, and nobody can tell me what "good" looks like. New graduates hear a third: every job post says AI PM, and the requirements look like three jobs at once.

There is an AI product manager career path, but it is not a single ladder. Titles vary by company. There is no guaranteed route into the role,

items.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
items.pt: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement

items.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
items.pt: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. items.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
items.pt: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile
